Kalsyto / Lake Federation (J33)

Region (English survey classification): Forbidden Plains.

In one sentence: debate, campaign and survive crises within a league of lake cities, then carry democracy, factories and firearms across Halann.

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 91/100 | Autocracy 12/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 20/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 65/100) | Pluralism 86/100. The inherited v2.1 value assessment is Good (78/100), with a stable trajectory. Poverty relief, opposition to slavery, protection of the vulnerable and recognition of peoples regarded as monstrous have specific mission-text support; parliament alone earns no credit. Exporting republicanism by force lowers restraint, so the assessment is qualified rather than unreserved.

Story: high | Mission-tree length: long (60 direct J33 definitions; pre-unification shared Federation missions counted separately) | Verified version: local Mod supports EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: exceptionally high | Forced waiting/grind: high (unification gates, Federation crises and parliament) | Early pressure: medium–high | Expansion capacity: exceptionally high.

The league in 1444 is not J33

The cities around the three lakes established their federation in response to past invasions, internal conflict and fear of tyrants. The offline English Wiki dates the league's formal ratification to 1441, presenting it as a commitment to collective defence and to preventing another “Tyrant Queen.” This helps explain its elaborate common institutions at the start. In 1444, however, the player selects a particular city-state, not unified Kalsyto. The current decision requires Federation membership, leadership, Kalyin Worship, constitutional conditions and sufficient cohesion before changing the country to Kalsyto, J33. Which city achieves this depends on the campaign; neither First City nor another particular member can be designated the sole predecessor.

Even before unification, the campaign differs sharply from ordinary territorial expansion. Rights to wage internal war, the status of leader and member, religious disputes, crises and constitutional choices matter more than grabbing land. The lake peoples' many languages and three-goddess faiths gradually become connected through the unifying conception of Kalyin. The offline Wiki gives a later setting chronology in which a constitution is adopted and the country unified in 1625; the game decision does not make 1625 the only possible formation date, and campaigns can produce different constitutions. The encyclopedia therefore strictly separates “the league exists” from “J33 has been created.”

The league is not naturally harmonious. The Zabatlari, Metsamic and Khamgunai peoples carry different memories, while their cities have divergent commercial and military interests. Shared fear of the steppe centaurs encourages cooperation, but does not automatically settle who leads, which faith speaks for everyone, or who provides taxes and soldiers. You may spend a long time building cohesion; you may also feel capable of defeating external enemies while still having to persuade your neighbours first. This political process is what players mean by the lengthy pre-unification phase.

One country, many possible federations

Formation of J33 does not end the story. Six constitutional options and parliamentary factions shape the priority given to industry, trade or the military; issues, factional influence and reform keep internal negotiation alive. The dedicated missions progress from defending the lakes, driving back steppe threats, mining and industrialisation to trading fleets, firearms, intercontinental diplomacy and the export of republican government. You can build a strong lake heartland and establish comparatively autonomous democratic subject states, turning the anti-tyrant ideal into a global political project. Magic and Kalyinite theology matter, but politics, industry and military technology dominate the core loop; this is not simply a mage state.

Mission titles already reveal the two sides of that national vision. “No One Left Behind” and “Those Deemed Monsters” point toward social inclusion, while “Ignite Blackpowder” and “Make Them Equal” place equality and force in the same frame. Parliament may prioritise trade or workshops, or give the military an important factional role. These are differences of political emphasis, not a promise that one campaign can realise every constitution's ideal outcome simultaneously. Recording J33 as liberty-oriented and pluralist while also rating warfare highly preserves that coexistence.

This country loudly proclaims equality, but that does not automatically earn a perfect value assessment. Local mission prose supports poverty relief, education, protection of the vulnerable and inclusion of peoples deemed monstrous within a common theology. It also contains coercion and militarism in exporting institutions by force and dealing with hostile societies. The inherited assessment is provisionally Good, with that tension retained: republican titles and anti-autocratic slogans earn no credit on their own; actual public policy and recognition of personhood do. A further source limitation matters here: the current “Wrong World” mission description explicitly calls for removing centaurs from the face of Halann. This is more severe language than the Chinese overview's general warning about coercion; its execution conditions and consequences were not fully audited for this translation. It must not be taken as proof of universal inclusion, nor silently used here to recalculate the frozen score. Player discussions are likewise divided: some enjoy the vast democratic-conquest campaign, while others find the pre-unification waiting and crises damaging to its pacing. Those are experiences of particular versions and routes.

This campaign suits players who enjoy political simulation, federal rivalries, constitutional factions, industrialisation and the long-term spread of an ideology. If you dislike spending a long time integrating city-states before expanding from a regional power into an intercontinental one, J33 will feel slow and intricate. The offline Wiki's later unification narrative enriches the setting; it does not replace current decisions or missions.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Kalsyto (J33) — Triunic Ideas

Set ID: J33_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = J33
    }

Triunic Traditions

  • Sailor Modifier: +20% (global_sailors_modifier; raw value 0.2).

  • Improve relations: +25% (improve_relation_modifier; raw value 0.25).

1. Back to the Motherlands

With our people united in purpose and spirit, we are ready to retake our ancient homelands in the plains, and to expand our grand union to lands beyond.

  • Settler growth: +1500% (global_colonial_growth; raw value 15).

  • Colonists: +1 (colonists; raw value 1).

2. Legacy of the Joglik Ut

The Joglik Uts, with their legendary ability to secure our homes from the centaurs over the centuries, have greatly inspired the military practices the Federal Guardsmen now use. The preservation of life is highly prioritized within our ranks, and in more recent years the Orachav have enabled us to adapt to the steppe whcih contrasts greatly from Yarikhoi.

  • shock_damage_received：-15% (shock_damage_received; raw value -0.15).

3. Federal Trade Guild

The formerly disunited and selfish trade leagues of the cities have been centralized into a single department, ensuring our merchants are fully capable of directing trade to our bustling markets.

  • Number of merchants: +1 (merchants; raw value 1).

  • Trade steering: +20% (trade_steering; raw value 0.2).

4. Birthplace of Democracy

When our ancestors overthrew the Tyrant Queen, they did not seek to make history. Nonetheless it was with her fall that some of the first republics in the world were founded as the bounds of monarchism were cast down. While others may predate the Day of Ashen Skies, none still remain to contest our legacy as the longest enduring democratic tradition.

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Horde unity: +1 (horde_unity; raw value 1).

  • Devotion: +1 (devotion; raw value 1).

5. The Price of a Mile

Many other countries ask what the price of a mile is, a way to discourage war and the ensuing devastation. Our soldiers however know damn well what the price is and are ready to pay it tenfold for the glory of the Federation.

  • Army morale: +10% (land_morale; raw value 0.1).

  • Reserves Organisation: +10% (reserves_organisation; raw value 0.1).

6. The Amber League

Our greatest academies have joined together into a unified scholarly institution, encouraging the education of our people and studies of the world.

  • Technology cost: -5% (technology_cost; raw value -0.05).

7. Children of the Lake

Even as our borders stretch far beyond the horizon we must not forget the waters that protected us from the centaurs and allowed our cities to thrive. We are the children of the lakes, and masters of the seas.

  • Naval leader manoeuvre: +1 (leader_naval_manuever; raw value 1).

  • Naval Morale: +10% (naval_morale; raw value 0.1).

Triunic Ambition

  • Governing Capacity Modifier: +15% (governing_capacity_modifier; raw value 0.15).
